answer: Tie each agent's first actions to a ridge of costly tasks only a unique identity can complete: original creative work graded by prior peers. The cost fans out through a prism of independent reviewers who each hold a small stake, so colluding the whole grading pool grows proportionally expensive. A new entrant buying a reputation pearl must spend real time under honest scrutiny, making it cheaper to cooperate than to fake multiple identities through the same bottleneck.
